bottom_line: In PEACE, trandolapril vs placebo did not reduce the primary end point (hazard ratio, 0.96; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.88 to 1.06; P=0.43).
implications: Given the primary end point incidence of 21.9% vs 22.5% with a hazard ratio of 0.96 (95% CI, 0.88 to 1.06; P=0.43), these data do not support a reduction in the composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or coronary revascularization with adding trandolapril in this studied population; the confidence interval includes no effect and does not exclude modest benefit or harm within its bounds.

major_points.text: Double-blind, placebo-controlled trial randomizing 8290 patients to trandolapril 4 mg/day target dose vs placebo.
major_points.quote: The trial was a double- blind, placebo-controlled study in which 8290 patients were randomly assigned to receive either trandolapril at a target dose of 4 mg per day (4158 patients) or matching placebo (4132 patients).

major_points.text: Primary end point was a composite of CV death, nonfatal MI, or coronary revascularization, with no significant difference between groups.
major_points.quote: The incidence of the primary end point — death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, or coronary revascularization — was 21.9 percent in the trandolapril group, as compared with 22.5 percent in the placebo group (hazard ratio in the trandolapril group, 0.96; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.88 to 1.06; P=0.43)
over a median follow-up period of 4.8 years.

major_points.text: Trandolapril reduced blood pressure more than placebo at 36 months (between-group difference statistically significant).
major_points.quote: After 36 months, the pressure had decreased by 1.4±0.3/2.4±0.2 mm Hg in the placebo group and by 4.4±0.3/3.6±0.2 mm Hg in the trandolapril group.

major_points.text: More discontinuations due to side effects occurred with trandolapril than placebo.
major_points.quote: Side effects leading to discontinuation of the study medication occurred in 6.5 percent of the patients in the placebo group and 14.4 percent of those in the trandolapril group (P<0.001).

major_points.text: Cough and syncope were more frequent with trandolapril than placebo.
major_points.quote: The rates of cough (39.1 percent vs. 27.5 percent, P<0.01) and syncope (4.8 percent vs. 3.9 percent, P=0.04) were greater in the trandolapril group than in the placebo group.
